newsitem.title: UK: Latam oil firms tiptoeing into N. Sea - consultant.
newsitem.headline: Latam oil firms tiptoeing into N. Sea - consultant.

text.p: Latin American state oil firms, keen to diversify away from their home base, may well follow the example of Canadian firms and become the latest investors to tap into the North Sea offshore industry.
In an interview with Reuters, Richard Wilson, oil industry consultant at Ernst & Young Energy Partners, said he expected firms such as Petrobras from Brazil to move in within the next five years.
"There are a number of state oil companies, such as in South America, who are contemplating investing outside their home country," said the Ernst & Young partner.
But he expects any newcomers to start cautiously, buying into mature oil field interests, which long-established players here want to divest, rather than make outright acquisitions.
"It is more likely to be through targeting specific fields or packages of fields, rather than companies," he said.
While Asian state oil companies show little interest, Wilson also expects Canadian firms to remain active in the North Sea after Talisman Energy Inc bought Goal Petroleum Plc about a year ago.
Gulf Canada Resources Ltd followed suit last week when it launched a bid for Clyde Petroleum Plc.
"Talisman has played a leading role and that has made most of them (Canadian firms) look at the North Sea," said Wilson.
Many Canadian companies traditionally were active onshore only and may see the North Sea as a relatively risk-free area to venture into offshore operations, he added.
A benign British tax regime is seen as a further incentive for Canadian firms to eye the other side of the Atlantic Ocean, Wilson said.

To take advantage of this flurry of corporate activity in the exploration and production sector, Ernst & Young recently announced an alliance with a geoscience consultancy -- IKODA -- and a broker in oil fields -- Hannon Westwood Associates.
"We want to be a one-stop shop for the oil industry," Wilson said.
The three-way co-operation does not involve any financial ties.
